problem.title: A composite integer passing the frozen BPSW-SL-1000 probable-prime procedure
problem.informal_statement:
Find a composite positive integer n on which one exactly specified Baillie-PSW variant returns PROBABLE_PRIME. The variant is frozen and named BPSW-SL-1000: trial division by every prime below 1000, a base-2 strong probable-prime test, a perfect-square exclusion, Selfridge Method A discriminant selection with P = 1 and Q = (1 - D)/4, and the strong Lucas test. The precise variant is part of the statement, not an implementation detail: changing the trial-division bound, the base, the discriminant rule, or the Lucas variant defines a different problem.

No witness is known to this definition and none may exist. The realistic deliverable is therefore a certified extension of the search frontier over exactly defined regions and families, each replayable from its frozen definition, and that negative outcome is retained as a first-class artifact rather than treated as failure. All arithmetic is exact integer arithmetic; no floating point appears on any trust path.

target_claim.statement: There exists a composite positive integer n, that is an n admitting integers a, b with 1 < a <= b < n and n = a*b, such that the procedure BPSW-SL-1000 returns PROBABLE_PRIME on input n. BPSW-SL-1000 is defined on integers n >= 2 with verdict alphabet PRIME, COMPOSITE, PROBABLE_PRIME, PARAMETER_DEGENERATE, using exact integer arithmetic only, as follows. Step 1: if n < 1000, trial divide n by every integer 2 <= t <= isqrt(n) and return COMPOSITE if some t divides n, else PRIME. Step 2: for each of the 168 primes p < 1000 in increasing order, return COMPOSITE if p divides n. Step 3: write n - 1 = 2^s * d with d odd and s >= 1, set x_0 = 2^d mod n; if x_0 is 1 or n-1 continue, else for j = 1..s-1 set x_j = x_(j-1)^2 mod n and continue if some x_j = n-1, else return COMPOSITE. Step 4: if isqrt(n)^2 = n return COMPOSITE. Step 5: for i = 0, 1, 2, ... let D_i = (-1)^i * (2i+5), so the trial discriminants are 5, -7, 9, -11, 13, -15, ..., each congruent to 1 mod 4; compute the Kronecker-extended Jacobi symbol (D_i/n) exactly by quadratic reciprocity; if (D_i/n) = 0 and |D_i| < n return COMPOSITE because gcd(|D_i|, n) is a nontrivial divisor; stop at the least i with (D_i/n) = -1 and set D = D_i, P = 1, Q = (1 - D)/4, so that P^2 - 4Q = D. Step 6: let g = gcd(n, 2*Q*D); if 1 < g < n return COMPOSITE, and if g = n return PARAMETER_DEGENERATE, which is not a pass. Step 7: with U_0 = 0, U_1 = 1, V_0 = 2, V_1 = P and U_(t+1) = P*U_t - Q*U_(t-1), V_(t+1) = P*V_t - Q*V_(t-1), write n + 1 = 2^k * m with m odd and k >= 1; return PROBABLE_PRIME if U_m = 0 mod n or if V_(m*2^j) = 0 mod n for some 0 <= j <= k-1, else return COMPOSITE.

assumption_claims.statement: The frozen procedure is exactly the seven-step BPSW-SL-1000 written in the target claim, and no other procedure. Its four choices are load-bearing parts of the statement: the trial-division bound is every prime below 1000, the probable-prime test is the strong test to the single base 2, the discriminant rule is the signed sequence D_i = (-1)^i (2i+5) with P = 1 and Q = (1-D)/4, and the Lucas test is the strong one. Any procedure differing in any of the four defines a different problem.

For odd n >= 3 with n - 1 = 2^s * d and d odd, n is a strong probable prime to base 2 iff 2^d = 1 mod n or 2^(d*2^j) = n-1 mod n for some 0 <= j <= s-1. This is step 3 and is not the Fermat condition 2^(n-1) = 1 mod n.

The frozen discriminant rule takes the least i >= 0 with Jacobi symbol (D_i/n) = -1 where D_i = (-1)^i (2i+5), then sets P = 1 and Q = (1-D)/4. Every D_i is congruent to 1 modulo 4 so Q is an integer, and P^2 - 4Q = D. Here (D/n) is the Kronecker-extended Jacobi symbol for odd n > 0 and any integer D, computed exactly by the binary reciprocity algorithm with (D/n) = (-1/n)*(|D|/n) for D < 0 and (-1/n) = (-1)^((n-1)/2); the Legendre symbol is a rejected reading because it is undefined for composite modulus. The perfect-square exclusion of step 4 precedes this search because for a perfect square n no D_i has Jacobi symbol -1 and the search would not terminate. Rejected alternatives, each a different problem: a rule retrying D = 5 specially, a rule stepping |D| by 4, the extra-strong rule choosing P with ((P^2-4)/n) = -1 and Q = 1, and a rule ordering candidates by smallest |D|.

With Lucas sequences defined by U_0 = 0, U_1 = 1, V_0 = 2, V_1 = P and, for t >= 1, U_(t+1) = P*U_t - Q*U_(t-1) and V_(t+1) = P*V_t - Q*V_(t-1), and with n + 1 = 2^k * m where m is odd and k >= 1, n is a strong Lucas probable prime for parameters (P, Q) iff U_m = 0 mod n or V_(m*2^j) = 0 mod n for some 0 <= j <= k-1. Residues modulo the odd n are computed by the exact doubling identities U_(2t) = U_t*V_t and V_(2t) = V_t^2 - 2*Q^t together with U_(t+1) = (P*U_t + V_t)*inv2 mod n and V_(t+1) = (D*U_t + P*V_t)*inv2 mod n, where inv2 = (n+1)/2 is the exact inverse of 2 modulo n. Rejected readings: the standard Lucas condition U_(n+1) = 0 mod n, and the extra-strong condition which additionally requires V_m to be congruent to plus or minus 2.

n is composite iff there are integers a, b with 1 < a <= b < n and n = a*b; the reading 'not prime' is rejected because it would admit n = 1, and 'has two distinct prime factors' is rejected because it would exclude prime powers. A compositeness certificate is an exhibited factorization re-multiplied to n by exact big-integer arithmetic, with every factor strictly between 1 and n. A probable-prime test returning COMPOSITE, a library primality verdict, and an unre-multiplied printed factorization are all rejected as certificates.

'Passes the frozen test' means the procedure returns PROBABLE_PRIME. The verdict PARAMETER_DEGENERATE, reached when gcd(n, 2*Q*D) = n, is explicitly not a pass, and an input halting there is not a witness even though the procedure never called it composite.

Every step on a trust path uses exact integer arithmetic only. In particular isqrt is an exact integer square root and never a floating-point square root, no logarithm is used to size or bound a decision, and no floating-point value may enter a verdict, a certificate, or an exclusion record. Floating-point or model-suggested values may guide which region to search next and are labelled exploration-only.

Every strong probable prime to base 2 is a Fermat probable prime to base 2, that is 2^(n-1) = 1 mod n. This standard fact is what licenses the necessary-condition congruence filter used in the semiprime sub-slice; a filter that is not provably necessary would turn an exhaustive exclusion into a sampled one.

Because step 2 rejects every n with a prime factor below 1000, any witness is composite with all prime factors at least 1009, hence n >= 1009^2 = 1018081. The trial-division bound therefore changes the witness set and is part of the frozen statement rather than an optimization.

The planning notes report that no BPSW counterexample exists below 2^64. This is an untrusted candidate, is not a premise of any computation, and must be revalidated by the ADR-0055 pre-research re-check, which must also establish which BPSW variant the cited enumeration used, because a frontier for one variant is not a frontier for BPSW-SL-1000. Direct sweeping cannot revalidate it: reaching 2^64 by the bounded interval method would need about 1.8*10^12 windows of the frozen size.

The attribution of the name Selfridge Method A to the frozen discriminant rule, and the attribution of the strong Lucas definitions to Baillie and Wagstaff 1980, are untrusted recollections pending acquisition. If acquisition shows the name belongs to a different rule, the written content of BPSW-SL-1000 is unchanged and only the naming row is corrected.

The reported heuristic that counterexamples should be plentiful is untrusted and is exploration-only route guidance. It may inform the choice of which family to freeze next, and it must never filter candidates inside an already frozen family, because a heuristic filter silently converts an exhaustive exclusion record into a sampled one without changing its wording.

Do not repeat the route that reports a base-2 strong pseudoprime, a Lucas pseudoprime, a Carmichael number, or a pass under the extra-strong or standard Lucas variant as a witness for the frozen target. Each is a distinct recorded outcome. An unreplayed third-party primality or BPSW library verdict is likewise refused as a certificate: it is an untrusted candidate until the independent verifier recomputes every step from the frozen specification, and adopting such a library is separately a pinned-dependency decision.

Exhausting a frozen interval, a frozen construction family, or a frozen congruence-filtered range establishes exactly that no candidate in that region passes the frozen procedure, and nothing about any integer outside it. No such exhaustion may be promoted into a claim that no composite passes the frozen procedure, and failure of a search is never evidence for the negation of the target.

formalization.statement: exists n : N, n >= 2 and (exists a b : N, 1 < a and a <= b and b < n and n = a*b) and BPSW_SL_1000(n) = PROBABLE_PRIME, where BPSW_SL_1000 is the seven-step total procedure frozen in the target claim and evaluated in exact integer arithmetic
quantifiers: exists n in N with n >= 2, unbounded above
exists a, b in N witnessing n = a*b with 1 < a <= b < n
forall p over the 168 primes below 1000 in step 2
exists j with 1 <= j <= s-1 in step 3, where n - 1 = 2^s * d and d is odd
exists i >= 0 least with Jacobi symbol (D_i/n) = -1 in step 5, terminating for non-squares because step 4 precedes it
exists j with 0 <= j <= k-1 in step 7, where n + 1 = 2^k * m and m is odd

quantifier_mapping: a composite positive integer, unbounded above
the exhibited nontrivial factorization certifying that n is composite
introduced by the frozen variant; they have no counterpart in the source line
definition_mapping: the exactly specified Baillie-PSW probable-prime test
the seven-step procedure BPSW-SL-1000 written in the target claim and no other procedure
the procedure returns PROBABLE_PRIME; PARAMETER_DEGENERATE is not a pass
n = a*b with 1 < a <= b < n
an exhibited factorization re-multiplied to n by exact big-integer arithmetic
recomputation of every step from the frozen specification, with every recorded intermediate compared to a freshly computed one
assumption_delta: The source line fixes no trial-division bound, no base set, no discriminant rule, and no Lucas variant; this dossier fixes all four and each choice changes the target.
The bound 1000 is not cosmetic: it forces every witness to satisfy n >= 1009^2 = 1018081.
A distinct PARAMETER_DEGENERATE verdict is added so that the degenerate parameter case is neither a pass nor a compositeness claim.
If an acquired primary source fixes a different variant, the strength relation becomes unresolved and the target is re-frozen as a new dossier rather than adjusted in place.
edge_case_delta: Inputs below 1000 are decided by exact trial division and can never be witnesses.
Perfect squares are rejected in step 4 before the discriminant search, which is what makes that search terminate.
n = 1 is outside the procedure's domain and is not composite under the frozen definition.
An input halting with PARAMETER_DEGENERATE is recorded as such and is not a witness.

success_criteria: an exhibited composite n with an exact nontrivial factorization re-multiplied to n and a fully replayed PROBABLE_PRIME transcript under the frozen BPSW-SL-1000 procedure
a rigorous proof that no composite positive integer passes the frozen BPSW-SL-1000 procedure
or an explicit unresolved outcome carrying a replayable certified exclusion record and a statement of the smallest remaining obligation
stopping_rules: stop on an exact certificate: a certified composite witness whose frozen-test transcript replays step by step
stop when the fresh model spend reaches USD 25
stop when two consecutive review points close no obligation and add no new certified exclusion region
never promote exhaustion of a frozen interval or of the frozen construction family into any claim that no composite passes the frozen procedure
halt and re-freeze rather than continue if a candidate passes a BPSW variant other than the frozen one
